page.layout: One page of text, set as one block of verse lines in italic, with a closing initial line "P.N.D." set right-aligned below the last line; no margin notes, no running head on the left beside the printed title "IBERICA" at the head, page number "27" at the top right.

main_text.p: Testetur vt se sanguine Hispano Satam: Certè vel illum fulminis, ceu Romulum, Perdet trisulci flamma: vel seu Dathanum Viuum de hiscens terra gurgite hauriet: Vel inter vrsos, Intuens terram, feras Villis opertus, huc & huc vagabitur Vt quem superba vox in has angustias Conjecit olim vindicante Numine. At tu, feracem quæ regis Britanniam, Dilecta cælo, gratias libans Deo, Perge, & superbos sternere ad terram duces Pacemque redde concidenti Galliæ, Repone regis in manu Sceptrum mei, Quod fœderatos inter, expetit sibi, Suaque proli, flamma regni Guisius. Redde & salutem te vocanti Belgio. Et nos canamus optimo laudes Deo, Qui fregit regis efferi superbiam Cælo minantis & piorum cœtui. Graues ruinas ille fœderis caput Telo petiuit, hinc minoribus necem Membris daturus, & tuis finem malis. O quæ tuorum fles acerba funera Amata Christo sponsa, nunc iacens humi, Miffura quondam sub iugum malis tuis Olim futura terror hostibus grauis, Olim futura Solis orbe clarior.

page.notes: Printed text in italic throughout, with long s rendered as s. Several words are set with the printer's own spelling (e.g., "Testetur", "Perdet", "Viuum", "Conjecit", "Missura"), kept as printed. The first line reads "Testetur vt se sanguine Hispano Satam:"; the scan's first word is set as printed "Testetur". Lines 1–2 of the verse are slightly uncertain: "Satam" and "Romulum" read clearly; "Certè" is printed with an acute accent over e as shown. The title "IBERICA" in capitals is a running head, not a heading. The closing "P.N.D." is an initialism for the author, set as its own paragraph. Word "Conjecit" line 8 may read "Conjecit" with a stroke over the second e; treated as printed.
